text:
sam: FYI customer escalation — acme-tools reporting p99 latency spike and 5xxs in hosted inference (usw2). SLO alert ~10m ago. Support seeing timeouts + some auth noise. Threading here to triage.
ops-bot: SLO Alert: hosted_infer_usw2.p99_latency > 500ms (10m) — alert id A-5921
lina: Thanks. Any customer IDs or example request ids we can query traces with?
sam: Cust: acme-tools. Support attached a request id and proxy logs. Example: request_id=01GZ9XKLT... and `POST /v1/generate -> 502 gateway timeout` repeated. Log: `2026-03-17T18:02:11Z proxy: upstream timeout after 12s`.
jules: Can you paste the request ids here so I can pull traces?
sam: pasted the id above and uploaded support zip.
maria: I see a short window of 5xxs around 18:00 UTC on the logs. Prefetch/handshake failures ticked up on probes. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/ingress-usw2
kevin: Any recent config or deploys? Could be an accidental change.
lina: Tracing shows a lot of trace gaps — spans stop at the gateway for many requests. Some logs show `auth: invalid_token` but customers report timeouts more than auth rejects.
sam: Support says customer rotated keys earlier; some clients may still try old keys. But that should be 401s. They report timeouts and retries causing longer tail.
maria: Batcher queue depth spiked at same time. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~85% to ~10% during spike — huge extra load on runtime.
jules: Running ad-hoc log query: `logs | where timestamp > '2026-03-17T18:00:00Z' and service='ingress' and status>=500 | top 100 by count` shows mix of 502/504/500 and many `upstream: connection reset` and `upstream: handshake timeout`.
lina: We pushed a prefetch TTL change yesterday — #4123 lowered prefetch TTL 5m -> 30s. That could explain cache churn.
kevin: Confirmed deploy: deploy/hosted-infer-config at 2026-03-17T17:45Z by ci-bot. Change: `prefetch_ttl=30s`.
sam: That aligns with the timeline. Lower TTL -> more backend hits -> increased contention -> timeouts.
maria: Also noted an auth-service rate-limit spike in the same window; some token validations were throttled which may have caused gateway fallback behavior.
jules: Common log samples include `proxy: upstream write failed: broken pipe` and `runtime: queue full`. Sounds like queue saturation and backend handshake failures.
sam: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) rollback prefetch TTL to 5m canary in USW2, 2) advise customer to backoff retries and confirm key rotation, 3) temporarily throttle heavy tenants (acme-tools) if they keep hammering.
lina: I'll run a replay in staging with low TTL to reproduce the effect on batcher + cache. Also start capturing higher sample rates for traces from acme-tools.
kevin: I'll push a canary rollback for prefetch TTL to 5m to a small subset of hosts in USW2 and monitor p99 and KV miss rate.
maria: I added a dashboard panel correlating KV miss rate, batcher depth, and p99 SLO. Enabled extra tracing sampling for acme-tools to catch spans past the gateway.
jules: After rollback canary started at 18:20, p99 improved ~75% by 18:27 on canary hosts.
ops-bot: Deploy rollback initiated: deploy/hosted-infer-config-rollback at 2026-03-17T18:21Z by kevin.
kevin: Canary looks good, rolling out full revert to USW2. Watching for any auth anomalies during change.
lina: Follow-ups: add a presubmit load test that simulates heavy fanout + short prefetch TTL to catch these regressions. Also add a guardrail in config validation to warn when prefetch TTL < 2m.
maria: For the postmortem I'll collect: traces (we boosted sampling), batcher metrics, KV cache metrics, deploy timeline, and support ticket text. Starting the incident doc now.
support-bot: Ticket #45789 updated: customer acme-tools notified of mitigation and we requested they validate key usage and reduce retry rate.
sam: Thanks team. Kevin/Lina, please ping oncall if anything changes. We'll close once postmortem doc linked and customer confirms stable.
